question:
I always enjoy reading your novels!

I've always been impressed by your choice of words and expressions, the structure of your writing, and your vocabulary. How did you develop all of that?
answer:
I think that if you've spent a long time reading lots of books because you genuinely enjoy it, rather than reading with the intention of studying, all of that will naturally accumulate within you.

I've always liked reading, but I'm really bad at reading books for the purpose of studying, and I wasn't particularly good at studying in general. I simply read books because I enjoyed them. And by “books,” I don't just mean novels—I think manga, games, or anything else is fine.

I think everyone remembers things they enjoyed, and I feel that the accumulation of all those enjoyable experiences has helped me with what I produce now as a novelist.

I think the fact that enjoying yourself can count as studying is probably the biggest perk of being a novelist.
